findings.title: CapitalFeasibility collapses two caller keys onto one capital level; the published §7 gate outcome flips between GO and CONDITIONAL_REVIEW on caller iteration order alone
findings.measured:
`__post_init__` rebuilds the mapping as `normalised[_level_key(level)] = ...`, and `_level_key` runs `calc(value)` then snaps onto DESIGN_CAPITAL_LEVELS. `calc` accepts str, int and Decimal, so `"1500000"` and `Decimal("1500000")` are two distinct keys in the caller's dict and one key afterwards. Nothing refuses; last one wins.

Same three-entry input, two orderings, driven through `emit_decision` on tests/integration/test_gate_validation.py's clean-run evidence (script: /Users/nimaalishahi/scratch-verify/decide.py):

  input A keys: ['1500000', Decimal('1500000'), Decimal('2000000')]
     excess_by_level : {Decimal('1500000'): Decimal('0.0362'), Decimal('2000000'): Decimal('0.0118')}
     capital feasible: True
     PUBLISHED OUTCOME: GO
     capital_feasibility_failed: False

  input B keys: [Decimal('1500000'), '1500000', Decimal('2000000')]
     excess_by_level : {Decimal('1500000'): Decimal('-0.0500'), Decimal('2000000'): Decimal('0.0118')}
     capital feasible: False
     PUBLISHED OUTCOME: CONDITIONAL_REVIEW
     capital_feasibility_failed: True

The correct behaviour on this input is a refusal: two entries name $1,500,000 and nobody can say which is the entry. Instead the −0.0500 measurement is deleted and the gate says GO.

The entry point has the *second* half of the same shape, and it is the exact spelling `pipeline.inputs.asset_pairs` was written to defeat one lane over — `assess_capital_feasibility` does `dict(excess_by_level)`, so a sequence of pairs is collapsed by `dict` before `__post_init__` can object:

  pairs = [(D('1500000'), D('-0.0500')), (D('1500000'), D('0.0362')), (D('2000000'), D('0.0118'))]
  -> excess_by_level: {Decimal('1500000'): Decimal('0.0362'), Decimal('2000000'): Decimal('0.0118')}  feasible: True

No test covers this: the only test touching `excess_by_level` keys is tests/hand_computed/test_gate_validation.py:343, and it uses one spelling per level.

The reporting lane got this right on the identical concept — `reporting.capital.level_key` (src/reporting/capital.py:83) *refuses* an unknown level, and `CapitalLadderReport.__post_init__` refuses a level reported twice. The arbiter's copy of the same function records silently and collapses silently.
findings.why_it_matters: `capital_feasibility.feasible` is read directly at src/gate_validation/decision.py:367 and decides GO vs CONDITIONAL_REVIEW. This is the class the commit set out to close (a caller-supplied identity key a boundary collapses silently, order-dependent survivor) sitting on the single most load-bearing published verdict in the repository, and the collapsing transformation here (`calc`) is wider than `normalise_asset` — it maps three source types onto one key space.
findings.suggested_fix: Give `CapitalFeasibility` the `asset_keyed` treatment: collect `(key, value)` pairs in the caller's order without letting `dict` see them (an `asset_pairs`-shaped helper, since `assess_capital_feasibility` currently accepts pairs), map each through `_level_key`, and raise on the collision rather than on the two values disagreeing — with a message naming both caller spellings, as `asset_keyed` does. `_level_key`'s docstring already states that the key space is the snapped one; the refusal is what makes that a fact rather than a description.

findings.title: matching_null._resolve_features silently drops a wallet's features when a mapping spells one address two ways — the sibling iterable branch of the same function refuses the identical input
findings.measured:
The mapping branch computes `key = (wallet or "").lower()` and assigns `records[key] = record`. Two mapping keys that differ only in case pass the self-consistency check (both records already carry the lowercased `wallet`, since `WalletFeatures.__post_init__` lowercases it), then collapse into one entry. The iterable branch, twelve lines below at :191, raises `ValueError("duplicate feature record for wallet ...")` on exactly the same data.

Universe ['0xs1','0xc1','0xc2','0xc3']; '0xc1' described twice, once with features identical to the selected wallet and once far away (script: /Users/nimaalishahi/scratch-verify/mn.py):

  order A  features keys ['0xC1','0xc1','0xs1','0xc2','0xc3']
     chosen primary control: 0xc2, distance 0.082463028773318837072514192349753620001
     balance SMD capital_deployed: -0.027487676257772945690838064116584539999

  order B  features keys ['0xc1','0xC1','0xs1','0xc2','0xc3']
     chosen primary control: 0xc1, distance 0E-38
     balance SMD capital_deployed: 0E+37

  same five records passed as an iterable -> ValueError: duplicate feature record for wallet 0xc1

A different control is matched, a different standardisation is computed over the universe, and a different §6.6 covariate-balance SMD is published — from one input, on iteration order.

No test exercises the duplicate through the mapping branch (`grep -rn "duplicate feature" tests/` returns nothing).
findings.why_it_matters: This is the class in its purest form: one function, two accepted input shapes, one of which refuses the collision and one of which resolves it by iteration order. The matched sets it produces are the input to §8's permutation null and therefore to the calibrated threshold, and the balance table is a published §6.6 figure. The module's own docstrings are emphatic that the result must be 'a function of the data alone' — matching.py:296 sorts the universe precisely so a caller's ordering cannot move the last digit of a standard deviation, while this line lets a caller's ordering choose the control outright.
findings.suggested_fix: In the mapping branch, refuse when `key` is already in `records`, with the same message the iterable branch raises — or better, funnel both branches through one collision-refusing collector so the two shapes cannot drift apart again. As with `asset_keyed`, refuse on the collision rather than on the two records disagreeing.

findings.title: DiagnosticPack's duplicate-scope refusal is defeated by respelling one capital level, because _scope_key keys on str(Decimal) rather than on the snapped level
findings.measured:
`_scope_key` renders the capital level as `str(scope.capital_level)`. `Decimal("1500000")` and `Decimal("1.5E+6")` are equal and hash equal but render as '1500000' and '1.5E+6', so two scopes that name the same measurement produce two different identity keys (script: /Users/nimaalishahi/scratch-verify/scope.py):

  scope keys: ('ethereum', 1, 'selected', '1500000', None, None)
              ('ethereum', 1, 'selected', '1.5E+6',  None, None)

  DiagnosticPack(items=(buy_win_rate@1500000 = 0.61, buy_win_rate@1.5E+6 = 0.19))
  -> ACCEPTED, both published:
       buy_win_rate capital_level= 1500000  value= 0.61
       buy_win_rate capital_level= 1.5E+6   value= 0.19

  Control, identical spelling -> UnknownDiagnostic ("appears twice for the same scope")

The published pack therefore carries two answers to one question — the thing __post_init__'s message says 'nothing is permitted to' choose between.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the same defect the two `level_key` helpers exist to prevent — gate_validation/windows.py:298 and reporting/capital.py:83 both snap a level onto the pre-registered constant, and both docstrings cite `Decimal("1.5E+6")` vs `Decimal("1500000")` by name as the reason. `DiagnosticScope` runs `calc` on the level but never snaps it, so the one identity key built from it is unstable under an equality-preserving respelling. It is the inverse of the collapse rather than the collapse itself — one measurement becomes two entries instead of two becoming one — but it is the same failure to give an identity key a canonical form.
findings.suggested_fix: Have `DiagnosticScope.__post_init__` snap `capital_level` through `reporting.capital.level_key` (which already refuses a level outside §3.1's five), or at minimum normalise the exponent before `_scope_key` renders it.

findings.title: derive_child_seed flattens (commit, purpose, index) into a pipe-joined string, so two distinct purposes can derive one seed
findings.measured:
`message = "{}|{}|{}".format(commit, purpose, index)` is not injective when a component contains the delimiter (script: /Users/nimaalishahi/scratch-verify/misc.py):

  derive_child_seed(master, commit='abc|null.leader', purpose='window1',        index=0)
    -> 91057054122863460495179724698494709738616472449431008072485148703461237999389
  derive_child_seed(master, commit='abc',             purpose='null.leader|window1', index=0)
    -> 91057054122863460495179724698494709738616472449431008072485148703461237999389
  SAME SEED FOR TWO DISTINCT (commit, purpose) PAIRS: True

The docstring three lines above asserts the opposite: 'Distinct purposes must never collide, so this string is part of the derivation, not a comment.'
findings.why_it_matters: Reported as an observation, not a defect with a reachable consequence: the callers I traced build purposes from `null_purpose(column, window)` (permutation.py:88, 'null.{column}.window{n}') and commits are hex, so no live caller can put a '|' in either component. It is listed because it is the same shape as the rest — a compound identity key flattened into one scalar by a transformation that is not injective — and because `permutation_null_detail` at matching.py:385 relies on seed distinctness as a checked invariant, so the claim in the docstring is currently unbacked rather than merely unreachable.
findings.suggested_fix: Length-prefix or hash each component (e.g. hmac over `b"".join(len(x).to_bytes(4,'big') + x for x in parts)`), or state in the docstring that the components must not contain '|' and check it in `_require`.

summary: I read the commit and swept the whole tree for the shape it names, then measured each candidate against the real entry points. The four keys the commit claims to have closed hold up: I probed `asset_keyed`/`asset_pairs` with bytes keys, `int`/`None`/`False`/`\"\"` keys, a three-way NATIVE_ETH/WETH/UPPER-WETH collision, an OrderedDict, a `dict` subclass with a lying `items()`, an `abc.Mapping` with a custom `items()`, a generator of pairs, and an object whose `.items` is a non-callable attribute — every one of them refuses (only an `int` key escapes as a raw `AttributeError` from `normalise_asset` rather than a typed refusal, and a `str` subclass with a lying `lower()` produces a dead entry rather than a collapse). The class, however, is not closed. I found it open in two more places and measured both: `gate_validation.CapitalFeasibility` collapses two caller keys onto one capital level and flips the published gate outcome between GO and CONDITIONAL_REVIEW on iteration order alone, and `matching_null._resolve_features` silently drops a wallet's features in its mapping branch while its own iterable branch refuses the identical input. Two smaller items of the same family are reported below. The tree is clean; all scratch work is under /Users/nimaalishahi/scratch-verify/.

I reconstructed each admitted residue against the composed run (`pipeline.run_wallet_window`) and measured the published output — `buy_quality`, the §10 realized/marked/dead mix, the census, the quarantine queue and the coverage report — for every one. Five of the six admissions are accurate: the ETH-sentinel rewrite is genuinely loud (netting quarantine, published score unchanged), the padded token quarantines at `_bucket_for` or lands the sell's book in the FIFO queue, the bypassed-hash double-count really does yield 0.75 and not 2 (verified with the subclass bypass, the `object.__setattr__` bypass, and a whitespace-padded variant the commit did not try), the mixed-case address rewrite is silent exactly as admitted, and a swapped `DiagnosticValue.amount` reaches the artifact but is refused by every gate entry point (`calc`, `evaluate_windows_detail`, `assess_capital_feasibility`) and yields a `SCHEMA` discrepancy in `_check_condition`. The sixth is not: "Nothing validates that an asset key is an address" is filed in `asset_keyed`'s docstring as the ordinary, benign case ("indistinguishable from a typo in the address itself"), but on `replacement_pools` an unreadable key produces the same `DEAD_ZEROED` / −100% / full-dead-share published number the same docstring calls "the worst of the four", with zero trace — and the fix is sitting in the data (`PoolState.asset`) unused. The adjacent case, a `pools` book whose key disagrees with the `PoolState` it holds, is not admitted at all and marks a position against the wrong pool: −0.25 against a true −0.5, the exact pair the commit cites as the defect it closed. No repo files were edited; `git status --short` is empty.

findings.title: A typo'd `replacement_pools` key publishes DEAD_ZEROED / −100% / dead_share 1 with no trace — the residue is admitted, but as the benign case, not as the "measured-looking zero" it actually is
findings.file: src/pipeline/inputs.py:118 (asset_keyed docstring, "Nothing here validates that a key is an address"); consumed at src/pipeline/run.py:716
findings.measured:
Constructed: one buy of 4,000 TOKEN_R for $1,000; primary pool POOL_R dead (quote reserve 1,000 raw, no swap for 2,592,000s); migration replacement POOL_M supplied with quote reserve 1.5e9 raw USDC, i.e. exit $750.

  replacement_pools={TOKEN_R: POOL_M}      -> return_pct -0.2500000000000000, basis LIQUIDITY_BOUND,
                                              buy_quality -0.25000000000000000000000000000000000000,
                                              shares r/m/d = 0 / 1 / 0, marked_usd 750, dead_usd 0
  replacement_pools={TYPO_R: POOL_M}       -> return_pct -1, basis DEAD_ZEROED,
                                              buy_quality -1, shares r/m/d = 0 / 0 / 1,
                                              marked_usd 0, dead_usd 1000.000000

where TYPO_R = TOKEN_R with the last hex digit changed (`0xc1…c1c2` vs `0xc1…c1c1`) — a valid-looking address, no padding, no collision, so `asset_keyed` accepts it. The wrong run's published surface is otherwise identical to the right one's: census {'VALID_BUY': 1}, quarantine [] (empty), CoverageReport(notional_usd_total=1000.000000, notional_usd_quarantined=0, notional_usd_scored=1000.000000, transactions_priced=1, transactions_unpriced=0). The only field that moves is the number itself and its §10 basis.

The position evidence positively asserts the false thing: `'replacement=none'`, `'cond3_no_validated_replacement=true'`, `'dead_pool=no_swap_for_30d+exit_below_minimum+no_validated_replacement'`. The caller supplied a replacement; the artifact says none existed. Contrast the correct run: `'venue_is_replacement=true'`, `'replacement_validated:0xb2b2…'`.

This is bit-for-bit the failure the commit measured for the checksummed key and closed (`test_a_checksummed_replacement_pool_still_follows_the_migration`, `-1` and full dead share against a true `-0.25`). Closing the case-variant spelling left the same published number reachable by an ordinary typo, and the docstring files that under the same sentence as "a price book listing a quote asset the window never traded" — which is genuinely benign, because a missing price is loud (measured below).
findings.why_it_matters: The three other unreadable keys are loud, so the admission's "this is the ordinary case" framing is right for them and wrong for exactly the one the same docstring earlier calls "the worst of the four, because the drop produces a measured-looking zero". Measured for comparison, same lot, same typo technique: typo'd `pools` key -> Stage.MARKING quarantine ("leaves an open position … and no pool state was supplied"), wallet unscorable, no number published; typo'd `token_starts` key -> Stage.MARKING quarantine ("no §4.7 token trading start"), wallet unscorable; typo'd `prices` key -> census {'UNSUPPORTED': 1}, wallet unscorable. Only `replacement_pools` converts an unreadable key into a full loss a reader would believe — §10's dead share is the basis the pre-registration most wants visible, and here it reports 100% of a position whose liquidity had merely migrated.
findings.suggested_fix: The check is available without validating that a key is an address: `PoolState` carries its own `asset`. In `WindowConfig.__post_init__`, refuse any `replacement_pools[key]` whose `normalise_asset(pool.asset) != normalise_asset(key)` — that catches this typo exactly (key `0x…c1c2`, `pool.asset == 0x…c1c1`) and every transposition, on the collision-style ground the commit already argues for (the entry is unreachable, so the mapping is one entry shorter than the caller believes). `marking.pools.validate_replacement` already applies the same identity rule one layer down (`normalise_asset(replacement.asset) != normalise_asset(pool.asset)` -> `replacement_rejected:token_identity_changed`); it simply never runs, because the lookup returned None. If a key that names a token the run never holds should stay legal, refuse only when the key disagrees with the value it holds — that is a statement about the mapping, not about the world.

findings.title: The pool book accepts a key that disagrees with the `PoolState` it holds, and marks the position against the wrong pool — silently, −0.25 against a true −0.5
findings.measured:
Constructed: one buy of 4,000 TOKEN_R for $1,000, marked at the horizon. Pool book with TOKEN_R's and TOKEN_H's *values* transposed while both keys stay correctly spelled and normalised — the ordinary shape of a mis-assembled join or an off-by-one zip:

  pools[TOKEN_R] = PoolState(POOL_R, asset=TOKEN_R, quote_reserve 1e9)   -> return_pct -0.500000000000000,
                                                                            buy_quality -0.50000000000000000000000000000000000001,
                                                                            marked_usd 500, venue=0xb1b1…
  pools[TOKEN_R] = PoolState(POOL_H, asset=TOKEN_H, quote_reserve 1.5e9) -> return_pct -0.2500000000000000,
                                                                            buy_quality -0.25000000000000000000000000000000000000,
                                                                            marked_usd 750, venue=0xb4b4…

Both runs publish census {'VALID_BUY': 1}, quarantine [] (empty), and the identical CoverageReport(notional_usd_total=1000.000000, notional_usd_trades=1000.000000, notional_usd_quarantined=0, notional_usd_scored=1000.000000, transactions_priced=1, transactions_unpriced=0). The §10 mix is identical in both (r/m/d = 0 / 1 / 0). Nothing distinguishes them but the return.

Directly confirmed that `_normalised_pools` accepts it: `_normalised_pools({TYPO_R: PoolState(asset=TOKEN_R, …)})` returns a book containing TYPO_R. The only per-entry check is `isinstance(pool, PoolState)`.

−0.25 against a true −0.5 is the same pair the commit message leads with ("two spellings of one token published -25% against a true -50%") as the defect it closed.
findings.why_it_matters: This is not in the residue list at all — neither `asset_keyed`'s docstring nor `_normalised_pools`'s mentions it, and `_normalised_pools`'s docstring claims the collision refusal is what stops "a different published return for the same input". The collision refusal closed the case where two keys name one asset; it did nothing about one key naming the wrong asset, which produces the same wrong published return by a route a caller is at least as likely to take (a transposed join is a more ordinary mis-assembly than supplying two spellings of one token). Unlike a mis-typed key, this one is not even detectably absent: the lookup succeeds, so no quarantine fires and no census line moves.
findings.suggested_fix: One line in `_normalised_pools`, beside the existing `isinstance(pool, PoolState)` loop: refuse when `normalise_asset(pool.asset) != normalise_asset(token)`. The pool states its own asset, so this asks the caller's mapping to agree with itself rather than asking anything about the world — the same ground `asset_keyed` already refuses on. Apply the identical rule to `WindowConfig.replacement_pools` (see the finding above); together they close both routes with one invariant.

findings.title: CONFIRMED ACCURATE: a rewritten token becomes a loud netting quarantine; a rewritten address is silently someone else's money
findings.file: src/pipeline/inputs.py:198 (ObservedTransaction docstring, "What that guarantees, and what it does not")
findings.measured:
Both halves of the admission constructed and run.

LOUD half — `object.__setattr__(leg, "token", NATIVE_ETH)` on a constructed `Transfer`, added to the control pair: quarantine [('netting', ('0xeth',), volume_usd=None)], census total 4 with quarantined=1, transactions_unpriced=1, and the published buy_quality is *unchanged* at 0.75000000000000000000000000000000000002 with shares 0.857…/0.142…/0. Genuinely loud, and the wrong row does not contaminate the number.

SILENT half — measured two shapes.
(a) Whole leg diverted: `object.__setattr__(leg, "to_addr", WALLET.upper())` on the TOKEN_R leg of buy 0xr in the control pair. Published buy_quality 2.0000000000000000000000000000000000001 against a true 0.75000000000000000000000000000000000002, and the §10 mix flips to realized/marked/dead = 1 / 0 / 0 — the highest credibility §10 can report — against a true 0.857…/0.142…/0. Quarantine empty. The census does carry a trace here (VALID_BUY 2 -> 1, ABOVE_TOLERANCE_RESIDUAL 0 -> 1), which is slightly *better* than admitted, though ABOVE_TOLERANCE_RESIDUAL is an ordinary data finding a reader would not read as input corruption.
(b) Sharper, and the one with no trace at all: a buy whose 4,000 tokens arrive in two 2,000-token legs, with one leg's `to_addr` rewritten to mixed case. The transaction stays a VALID_BUY. Published return −0.66666666666666666666666666666666666666 against a true −0.500000000000000; buy_quality −0.666… against −0.500…; open_raw 2000000000000000000000 against 4000000000000000000000. Census {'VALID_BUY': 1} in both, quarantine empty in both, §10 mix 0/1/0 in both, CoverageReport byte-identical in both. Zero trace.

Also verified the `type(item) is Transfer` claim (commit claim 4): a `@dataclass(frozen=True) class RawTransfer(Transfer)` with a no-op `__post_init__` carrying `token=NATIVE_ETH` is refused with "transfers[0] is a RawTransfer, not a contracts.Transfer"; a second-level subclass is refused too; `copy.deepcopy` of a genuine Transfer keeps `type(...) is Transfer`.
findings.why_it_matters: The admission is accurate as written — no correction needed. Recorded because the lens asked for the measurement, and because (b) is the version worth citing if anyone later argues the census would surface it: it does not.
findings.suggested_fix: None required. If it is ever revisited, the docstring already names the closure (re-derive each leg's normal form at the entry point) and the reason it was declined (it would make netting's own §4.2 refusal unreachable through the only route the composed pipeline has to it).

findings.title: CONFIRMED: the bypassed-hash residue yields 0.75, not 2 — including a whitespace variant the commit did not construct, where the stated FIFO refusal does not fire but the answer is still the distinct-hash answer
findings.measured:
Three bypasses run against `_colliding_pair("0xdup", "0xdup")`, all of which put an un-normalised hash past the duplicate check:

  subclass with no-op __post_init__, "0xDUP" -> buy_quality 0.75000000000000000000000000000000000002,
                                               shares 0.857…/0.142…/0, quarantine [],
                                               accounts '0xDUP' ret -0.5, '0xdup' ret 2
  object.__setattr__(tx_hash, "0xDUP")      -> identical, 0.75000000000000000000000000000000000002
  object.__setattr__(tx_hash, "0xdup ")     -> identical, 0.75000000000000000000000000000000000002

None reproduces the double-count (2, with realized_share 1). Structurally confirmed why: `contracts.Transaction.__post_init__` does *not* normalise `tx_hash` (it only re-tuples `transfers`), so the two spellings stay distinct in every hash-keyed structure below — `consumptions_by_buy`, `excluded_hashes`, `quarantined_txs`, `deferred_buys`. There is no downstream re-normalisation for the entry check to be out of step with, other than `fifo._require_a_total_order`'s `.lower()`.

One incompleteness in the stated mechanism, not in the conclusion. The commit says "where the two land in one lot book `fifo._require_a_total_order` lowercases, refuses, and the book goes to the queue naming both spellings." That holds for a case difference — two same-token buys as "0xDUP"/"0xdup" give quarantine [('fifo', ('0xDUP','0xdup'))], buys_scored 0. It does not hold for whitespace: `_require_a_total_order` does `(event.tx_hash or "").lower()` without `.strip()`, so "0xdup "/"0xdup" in one book is *not* refused — quarantine [], buys_scored 2, published buy_quality -0.49999999999999999999999999999999999999 with both lots marked at -0.5.

That published number is still the answer two genuinely distinct hashes would give for two distinct buys of 4,000 TOKEN_R at $1,000 each, so the load-bearing sentence ("A correct answer about an input that lied, or a loud quarantine — not a silent double-count") survives.
findings.why_it_matters: The critical case the lens flagged — that the commit understated its own worst residue — does not occur. Recorded so the next reader knows the whitespace variant was tried, and so the FIFO half of the sentence is not relied on as if it covered every un-normalised spelling: it covers case, not padding.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional and cosmetic: either narrow the sentence in `_require_one_transaction_per_hash` to "lowercases, so a case difference in one book is refused", or add `.strip()` alongside `.lower()` in `fifo.matching._require_a_total_order`'s key so the two normalisations agree. Neither changes any published number for a well-formed input.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: a swapped DiagnosticValue.amount reaches the artifact and no gate path reaches it
findings.measured:
Built `diagnostic("buy_win_rate", scope, Decimal("0.61"), kind=RATIO)` in a pack, then `object.__setattr__(d.value, "amount", Decimal("0.99"))`.

  pack.verify()                                 -> PASSES (rewrite not caught, exactly as admitted)
  canonicalise(d)                               -> {'value': {'amount': '0.99', 'kind': 'ratio'}, 'gate_relevance': 'DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY', …}
                                                   i.e. 0.99 reaches the published artifact in place of 0.61000000

Every gate surface fed the rewritten `d.value`:

  calc(d.value)                                 -> TypeError: cannot build a Decimal from DiagnosticValue
  evaluate_windows_detail([], d.value)          -> TypeError: cannot build a Decimal from DiagnosticValue
  assess_capital_feasibility({1500000: d.value})-> TypeError: cannot build a Decimal from DiagnosticValue
  check_validation_gate_detail({'golden_set_precision': d.value})
                                                -> Discrepancy(kind='schema', field='golden_set_precision',
                                                   detail='cannot build a Decimal from DiagnosticValue')

The retraction's stated reason holds under test: `_check_condition` calls `calc(value)` before any comparison, so an EXACTLY bar yields SCHEMA and never a held condition — the permitted `__eq__` is never reached. Checked the two other comparison routes too: `check_numeric_fields_detail` funnels through `calc` (SCHEMA); `check_exact_fields_detail` funnels through `_comparable` -> `canonicalise`, which renders a DiagnosticValue as a dict `{'amount': …, 'kind': …}` and so can never compare equal to a scalar field (MISMATCH, loud). `d.value.amount` is accepted by `calc` and returns Decimal('0.99') — the deliberate, documented escape, unchanged.
findings.why_it_matters: The one residue the module could not close is bounded exactly where it claims to be: report yes, gate no. No correction needed.

findings.title: CONFIRMED: a padded token in the transfer stream is loud on the buy side; on the sell side it leaves the wallet scored, but the queue and the wallet row both carry it
findings.file: src/pipeline/inputs.py:100 (asset_keyed, "A padded key is refused too")
findings.measured:
PAD = "  " + TOKEN_R + " ". Control: buy 4,000 TOKEN_R for $1,000, sell all for $1,500 -> buy_quality 0.50000000000000000000000000000000000001, shares 1/0/0, return +0.5.

  buy padded / sell plain  -> buy_quality None (wallet unscorable). Two quarantine records:
                              ('fifo', ('0xs',)) and ('marking', ('0xr',), "no §4.7 token trading start").
  both padded              -> buy_quality None. quarantine [('marking', ('0xr',))].
  buy plain / sell padded  -> buy_quality -0.50000000000000000000000000000000000001 against a true +0.5,
                              shares r/m/d = 0 / 1 / 0 against a true 1 / 0 / 0,
                              return -0.500000000000000 against +0.5.
                              quarantine [('fifo', ('0xs',))], and the wallet row carries
                              n_sells_quarantined = 1 beside the published score.

The reason the buy side is always loud is `_bucket_for`: `config.token_start(padded)` is None because `asset_keyed` refuses padded keys in `token_starts`, so every padded buy quarantines before it can reach a pool. The third shape is the one worth naming: the wallet stays scored and publishes a number that is wrong in sign and magnitude, so the trace is the queue record and the wallet's own `n_sells_quarantined`, not the absence of a score.
findings.why_it_matters: The admission ("still splits one asset into two across netting, FIFO and marking") is accurate and the outcome is loud in every shape — but 'loud' means 'a quarantine record beside a published score', not 'no number published', which is worth knowing before anyone relies on the sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: None. If it is ever tightened, the cheapest place is the same one `asset_keyed` argues against tightening — and its reason (trimming here would give the module a key space the seam does not have) still stands.

findings.title: OBSERVATION, not closable at this boundary: transposed `token_starts` values silently flip the §4.7 age bucket
findings.measured: Same buy of TOKEN_R. With the correct starts the account's bucket is TokenAgeBucket.D. Transposing TOKEN_R's and TOKEN_M's `TokenStart` values (both keys correctly spelled) gives TokenAgeBucket.A, with quarantine [] and buy_quality unchanged at -0.50000000000000000000000000000000000001.
findings.why_it_matters: The bucket feeds the Edge Origin condition, so a transposition moves a gate-adjacent classification with no trace. Unlike the pool book, `TokenStart` carries no asset field, so there is nothing at the boundary for the key to be checked against — this is a wrong value rather than a mis-keyed structure, and no seam can catch it. Recorded so it is not mistaken for the same class as the two pool-book findings, which are closable.
findings.suggested_fix: Nothing at this boundary. If it ever matters enough, `TokenStart` would need to carry the token it describes — a change to the shape of the input, not a check.

summary: I read the commit and its message, then measured rather than reasoned. Headline: **the fix does not break legitimate use and does not move a published number in the wrong direction.** I built a detached worktree of 2672eed^ and ran the same constructed scenarios through both trees. The composed day's pinned hash (341d0d11…) is unchanged, and every hash that moved moved in the intended direction only: checksummed pools/prices/token_starts now reproduce the baseline day exactly (parent published a *different* run, 492ac1e3…), and a checksummed replacement-pool key now publishes marked=$4,000 / return=+7.0 / dead_share=0 instead of the parent's dead=$500 / return=-1 / dead_share=0.0714 — the commit's claim, confirmed on the real numbers. `asset_keyed` refused nothing a legitimate caller would supply in my probes (empty, single-key, non-dict `Mapping`, `MappingProxyType`, already-normalised, bare sentinel with no WETH beside it, sentinel in any case, pair sequences, generators): values are returned by identity and first-appearance order is preserved. The published surface is order-invariant — 72 permutations of the pool/price/token_start key orders, 20 shuffles of the transaction order, and 4 `PYTHONHASHSEED` values all yield one hash, so no set or dict order leaks into a number. `type(item) is Transfer` accepts `dataclasses.replace`, `copy`, `deepcopy`, `pickle` and `Transfer(**asdict(t))` round-trips; the only Transfer subclass in the repo is the adversarial one in the tests. Suite: 1526 passed, 59 skipped; 48 dangerous + 1 equivalent mutation = the claimed 49; `ALLOWED` and `DEFERRED` are both empty. Tree left clean at 2672eed, worktree removed. Three minor things did turn up, all measured below; none is a wrong number today.

findings.title: A price book carrying ETH and WETH at the *same* price published the right answer before and is now a hard refusal of the whole run
findings.file: src/pipeline/inputs.py:131 (raise in asset_keyed), reached from src/pipeline/run.py:447
findings.measured:
Constructed input (the pinned integration day, `tests/integration/test_pipeline.py`), price book widened by one consistent row:

    run_wallet_window(the_day(), POOLS,
        {USDC: Decimal("0.000001"),
         WETH: Decimal("0.000000000000003"),
         NATIVE_ETH: Decimal("0.000000000000003")},   # same price, both spellings
        WINDOW, CONFIG)

At 2672eed^ (detached worktree): succeeds. `canonical_hash(summarise(result))` = `341d0d119f8ff236312c601a4c641709e73c4e459e2dee7b4fa0d1854469081e` — byte-identical to the baseline day's pinned hash. Every published number is the right one.

At 2672eed: `ValueError: prices names 1 asset(s) more than once: 0xc02aaa39b223fe8d0a0e5c4f27ead9083c756cc2 is named by 2 keys: '0xc02aaa39…', '0x0000…0000'`. No number is published at all.

Note `NATIVE_ETH` is the zero address `0x0000…0000`, so this is also the shape of any pool or price book that carries a zero-address placeholder row beside a real WETH row. The commit's own test for this case (`test_an_eth_row_beside_a_weth_row_in_the_price_book_refuses_the_whole_run`) uses *disagreeing* prices (0.0000000000000031 vs 0.000000000000003); the agreeing case — which is what a vendor table that quotes ETH and WETH consistently actually looks like — is the one that went from correct to refused, and it is not covered by a test.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the guard-that-refuses-valid-input shape the review lens exists to catch: a caller whose price table is internally consistent gets a run that will not start, and the obvious "fix" for the next person is to delete or weaken the guard — which would reopen the disagreeing case too, where the refusal is genuinely load-bearing. I do not think the guard is wrong (the docstring's argument that a disagreement-conditioned guard closes the instance and leaves the class open is sound), but the cost is real and undocumented in the message.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the refusal; make it actionable and pin the agreeing case. The message says what it will not do ("refused rather than resolved") but never tells the caller what to do — add one clause naming the remedy, e.g. "supply exactly one of these spellings; §4.2 makes them one asset, so the other row is redundant even when the two agree." And add a test asserting that ETH+WETH at the *same* price still refuses, so the next reader sees that the agreeing case is a deliberate cost rather than an oversight.

findings.title: The published report artifact changed shape — diagnostic payloads are now nested objects — while still stamping reporting_schema_version "report-v1"
findings.measured:
Same fixture (`tests/integration/test_reporting.py::_run()`), canonicalised under both trees:

  2672eed^   "value": "980000.25"                     (ranking row)
             "value": "0.184"                        (scalar diagnostic)
  2672eed    "value": {"amount": "980000.25", "kind": "usd"}
             "value": {"amount": "0.184", "kind": "ratio"}

  canonical_hash(_run()):
  2672eed^   f8201f26e1b2a125c2dec98ef7174e7a86b4a5b6895a60737ef46b308258783f
  2672eed    207d9dc17b559d1115eb7fe976e94b5b3b2556bac184978202c45ebceb3bfdef

  run.reporting_schema_version == "report-v1" in BOTH trees.

The amounts themselves are byte-identical ("980000.25", "0.184") — no measured figure moved. What moved is the artifact's structure and therefore its canonical hash, which `gate_validation/manifest.py` records and §9.6 pins.
findings.why_it_matters: Two artifacts that both declare `report-v1` are now structurally incompatible: a reader (or the gate-validation manifest check, which deliberately refuses to import `reporting` and works off the hash) cannot tell from the version stamp that the `value` field changed from a scalar to an object. `REPORTING_SCHEMA_VERSION` lives in `contracts/numeric.py`, i.e. inside the frozen seam, so this commit could not bump it — which is exactly why it should be recorded rather than left to be discovered. Nothing has been published yet, so the blast radius today is zero.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the pending version bump explicitly — a note in `src/reporting/run.py` or the freeze docs saying that `report-v1` no longer describes the diagnostics block and that `REPORTING_SCHEMA_VERSION` must go to `report-v2` the next time the seam is unfrozen. If the seam can be touched, bump it now; a version string that does not move when the shape moves is worse than no version string.

findings.title: DiagnosticValue breaks the __eq__/__hash__ contract and its equality is non-transitive
findings.measured:
a = DiagnosticValue(amount=Decimal("1"), kind="usd")
b = DiagnosticValue(amount=Decimal("1"), kind="ratio")
d = Decimal("1")

  a == d            -> True
  b == d            -> True
  a == b            -> False        # equality is not transitive
  hash(a) == hash(d)-> False
  len({a, d})       -> 2            # two slots for two objects that compare equal
  d in {a}          -> False        # while a == d is True
  a in [d]          -> True         # list membership uses ==, set membership uses hash

`__eq__` (line 344) returns `self.amount == other` for a bare `Decimal`/`int`, but `__hash__` (line 357) is `hash((DiagnosticValue, self.amount, self.kind))`, which can never equal `hash(Decimal("1"))`.
findings.why_it_matters: The docstring argues at length that equality is the one deliberate exception because "checking a rendered figure against an expected one is what a report is for" — but the exception as implemented makes `==` disagree with itself depending on which container asks. A reader who writes `assert d.value in EXPECTED_SET` gets False while `assert d.value == EXPECTED` passes, and the two `DiagnosticValue`s carrying the same amount at different scales both equal the same Decimal while not equalling each other. That is precisely the small, plausible-looking wrongness this repo is built to keep out of a comparison. Blast radius today is limited: `DiagnosticValue` is not used as a dict or set key anywhere in `src/`, so no published number is affected.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one. Either restrict `__eq__` to `DiagnosticValue` operands only (returning `NotImplemented` for `Decimal`/`int`), which keeps the hash consistent and costs callers one `.amount`; or keep the cross-type equality and make `__hash__` return `hash(self.amount)` so equal objects hash equally — noting that this then makes `a` and `b` (same amount, different kind) hash-collide but compare unequal, which is legal. The first is cleaner and matches the module's own "the number is not reached by accident" line.

findings.title: A non-string key in token_starts / replacement_pools now raises a bare AttributeError from inside the frozen seam
findings.measured:
WindowConfig(horizon_block=1, horizon_ts=1, token_starts={7: TokenStart(block=1, timestamp=1)})

  2672eed^   accepted -> {7: TokenStart(block=1, timestamp=1)}   (stored, unreachable by any lookup)
  2672eed    AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'lower'

The traceback surfaces from `contracts.normalise_asset`, not from this module, so it names neither `token_starts` nor the offending key. Every other refusal in `asset_keyed` and `WindowConfig.__post_init__` quotes the caller's own spelling deliberately ("the one they can search for").
findings.why_it_matters: Both behaviours are bad — the parent silently stored an entry nothing could read, the new one refuses with an error that points at the frozen seam rather than at the caller's mapping. No published number is involved, and no legitimate caller supplies an int key.
findings.suggested_fix: In the padding loop in `asset_keyed`, replace `text = key if isinstance(key, str) else ""` with an explicit refusal for non-str keys, in the same voice as the padding message: `{what}[{key!r}] is a {type} rather than a str; an asset key is an address and normalise_asset works on strings.` That is one branch and it keeps the module's rule that every refusal names the mapping and the caller's spelling.

summary: I read the full commit, reproduced its three quoted numbers by reverting the guards, and empirically tested every factual claim added or modified in its docstrings, comments and error messages. Most of the commit's claims hold under measurement: all six duplicate-hash shapes and all four asset-key collisions genuinely refuse; the three quoted figures (-25% vs -50%, $1,000,000,000 vs $1,000, DEAD_ZEROED/-100%/dead_share=1) reproduce exactly; `normalise_asset` really does not strip; `type(item) is Transfer` really does refuse every derivation in both base orders (metaclass and `__instancecheck__` routes do not work); `WindowConfig` really does normalise stored keys; `verify()` really does re-run each item's `__post_init__` (I swept 90+ constructed mutations across every field of every object in the tree and found zero misses); and `1526 passed, 59 skipped` reproduces. But the commit's stated purpose was to remove overclaimed docstrings, and it replaced two of them with new overclaims that are measurably false: the diagnostic payload is NOT refused at every gate entry point (`check_derived_fields` reads it as a number via `Decimal(str(...))` and holds), and `verify()` does NOT keep a rewritten diagnostic out of the artifact (it guards assembly, not publication). Two further claims are false in detail without a consequence: the `SCHEMA`-at-every-comparison claim, and "every leg was produced by `Transfer.__init__`".

findings.title: "both are refused at every gate entry point, because those all funnel through calc too" is false: check_derived_fields reads a DiagnosticValue as a number and the check HOLDS
findings.measured:
`gate_validation.check_derived_fields` delegates to `contracts.verify_redundant_derived`, which does `claimed = Decimal(str(claimed_raw))` (src/contracts/serialization.py:184) — not `calc`. `DiagnosticValue.__str__`, added by this commit, returns `format(self.amount, "f")`.

Constructed input:
    V = diagnostic("buy_win_rate", scope, D("0.61")).value      # DiagnosticValue(0.61000000, kind='ratio')
    recomp = {"total": lambda p: calc(p["a"]) + calc(p["b"])}
    gate_validation.check_derived_fields({"total": V, "a": "0.3", "b": "0.31"}, recomp)

Measured output:
    agrees   (a+b = 0.61)             -> 0 discrepancy(ies)          <-- the §9 check HELD on a DiagnosticValue
    disagrees(a+b = 0.62)             -> 1 discrepancy(ies)          <-- proves the number was genuinely read
    control: bare Decimal, agrees     -> 0 discrepancy(ies)
    control: bare Decimal, disagrees  -> 1 discrepancy(ies)
    contracts.verify_redundant_derived({'total': V, ...}, recomp) -> True
    calc(V) -> TypeError: cannot build a Decimal from DiagnosticValue

The payload behaves identically to the bare `Decimal("0.61")` it replaced, at an entry point exported from `gate_validation`. Right behaviour: either the sentence is narrowed to name the entry points that do funnel through `calc` (`_check_condition`, `evaluate_windows*`, `assess_capital_feasibility`, `check_numeric_fields`, `check_schema` — all four measured as refusing), or `verify_redundant_derived` uses `calc`. The same measurement also falsifies the narrower claim at diagnostics.py:52 — "Getting a gate-readable number out takes a second, differently-named step that says in the diff what it is doing": here the `str()` step happens inside the arbiter, with nothing in any diff. The repo's own sweep `test_no_attribute_of_a_diagnostic_carries_a_measurement_the_gate_would_accept` cannot see this because it probes `calc(attribute)` only, and the leak is through `Decimal(str(...))`.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the module's central thesis sentence and the reason the DiagnosticValue wrapper was introduced at all. A reviewer relying on it would believe a §10 diagnostic cannot satisfy a §9 artifact check; measured, it can — and it can do so silently, because the arbiter reports zero discrepancies.
findings.suggested_fix: Either route `verify_redundant_derived`'s `claimed_raw` through `contracts.calc` instead of `Decimal(str(...))` (the seam is frozen, so this may need to be a `_comparable`-style guard in `gate_validation.check_derived_fields`), or rewrite diagnostics.py:20-24 to name the entry points that do funnel through `calc` and state that `Decimal(str(...))` reads a `DiagnosticValue` as its figure.

findings.title: "This is what keeps a rewritten diagnostic out of the artifact" is false: verify() guards report_run, and run_artifact is the publication step
findings.measured:
The comment at src/reporting/run.py:157-160 says "Publication is the moment the invariant has to hold, and a pack constructed correctly can be rewritten afterwards ... This is what keeps a rewritten diagnostic out of the artifact." The matching claim is at src/reporting/diagnostics.py:512 ("refuse to *carry* an item whose invariants no longer hold, which is what stops a rewrite reaching an artifact") and the test is named `test_a_rewritten_diagnostic_cannot_be_published`. But `verify()` is called only inside `report_run`, and `run_artifact(report)` — the actual publication step — never calls it. Neither does `RunReport.__post_init__`.

Constructed input (route A — rewrite after report_run returns, the exact window the comment names, moved one step later):
    report = _run()                                   # tests/integration/test_reporting.py fixture
    scalar = [i for i in report.diagnostics.items if hasattr(i, "value")][0]
    object.__setattr__(scalar, "gate_relevance", "GATE")
    object.__setattr__(scalar, "name", "sharpe_ratio")   # not in DIAGNOSTIC_NAMES
    art = run_artifact(report)

Measured output:
    artifact carries: {"gate_relevance": "GATE", "kind": "ratio", "name": "sharpe_ratio", "scope": {...}, "value": {"amount": ...}}
    payload_hash: 1944bee2ab3be0d97f53b51bfc58e6897e866f291a37a29f22ff54b7fde75a71
    gate_validation.verify_envelope(art) -> []            <-- envelope verifies clean

Route B — `RunReport(...)` constructed directly (public, exported from `reporting`, used by the repo's own tests at tests/integration/test_reporting.py:616): built successfully with the tampered pack, and `"GATE"` reaches the artifact. Route C, the guarded one, behaves as claimed: `report_run(..., diagnostics=pack)` -> DiagnosticPromotionRefused.

So of three routes to a hashed artifact, `verify()` closes one.
findings.why_it_matters: A rewritten `gate_relevance` and an unregistered diagnostic name land in a hashed, envelope-verified artifact — the thing the whole DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY label exists to keep auditable. The comment tells the next reader the window is closed when it has only moved from before `report_run` to between `report_run` and `run_artifact`.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `self.diagnostics.verify()` from `RunReport.__post_init__` (which covers both routes and is what `run_artifact` consumes), or call it at the top of `run_artifact`. Then the comment is true as written; otherwise it should say it guards assembly, not publication.

findings.title: "a SCHEMA discrepancy ... whichever comparison the condition names" is false for the IS_TRUE condition
findings.measured:
The docstring says `_check_condition` "routes the reported figure through contracts.calc *before* it compares anything ... A DiagnosticValue in a gate report is therefore a SCHEMA discrepancy — the condition is recorded as unmeasurable, never as held — whichever comparison the condition names." But `_check_condition` (src/gate_validation/artifacts.py:719-725) handles `IS_TRUE` with `if value is True` *before* reaching `calc` at line 731.

Constructed input: a DiagnosticValue placed in every field of `VALIDATION_GATE_CONDITIONS + RECONCILIATION_CONDITIONS`.

Measured output — 15 of 16 conditions give `schema`; one does not:
    golden_set_precision                  ==       -> schema
    ...
    independent_review_completed          is_true  -> mismatch      <-- not schema, and calc was never called
    supported_transaction_coverage        ==       -> schema
    ...

The load-bearing half survives: no condition held (0 of 16). The repo's own test `test_equality_is_a_gate_rule_and_calc_is_what_keeps_a_diagnostic_out_of_one` asserts `[d.kind] == [SCHEMA]` only over the 10 `EXACTLY` conditions, so the docstring generalises past what was checked.
findings.why_it_matters: The commit message repeats this as one of its three headline corrections ("a diagnostic yields a SCHEMA discrepancy and never a held condition"). The safety half is true; the mechanism half is not, and a reader who trusts "routes the figure through calc before it compares anything" will mis-model the IS_TRUE branch.
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow to "whichever *numeric* comparison the condition names", and note that IS_TRUE compares by identity before `calc` and yields MISMATCH — still never a held condition.

findings.title: "every leg reaching a stage was produced by Transfer.__init__" is false by three routes that all satisfy type(x) is Transfer
findings.measured:
The paragraph's first half is true and I confirmed it: a plain subclass, `MI1(Transfer, Mixin)` and `MI2(Mixin, Transfer)` are all refused; a metaclass cannot make `type()` lie; `__instancecheck__` is irrelevant to `type() is`. But the guarantee sentence is false.

Route 1 — `object.__new__`, no constructor at all:
    raw = object.__new__(Transfer)
    for k, v in dict(token=NATIVE_ETH, from_addr="0xAbCdEf", to_addr="0xB", raw_amount=1, log_index=0, is_fee=False).items():
        object.__setattr__(raw, k, v)
    -> type(raw) is Transfer: True ; ObservedTransaction ACCEPTED it ; token = '0x0000...0000', from_addr = '0xAbCdEf'

Route 2 — `copy.copy` / `copy.deepcopy` / `pickle.loads` all go through `__reduce_ex__`, not `__init__`:
    copy     type is Transfer: True  token: '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'
    deepcopy type is Transfer: True  token: '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'
    pickle   type is Transfer: True  token: '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'
    (`dataclasses.replace` does re-run __init__: token collapses back to WETH.)

Route 3 — the sharpest, because it is the very subclass the docstring says is refused in any base order:
    leg = RawTransfer(token=NATIVE_ETH, from_addr=WALLET.upper(), ...)   # no-op __post_init__
    object.__setattr__(leg, "__class__", Transfer)
    -> type(leg) is Transfer: True ; ObservedTransaction ACCEPTED it ; token still the sentinel

Consequence measured through the composed run, and it is bounded to the residue the docstring already states: the sentinel route quarantines (`Stage.NETTING`, 1 record, "still carries the native ETH sentinel"), and the mixed-case-address route is silent — control `VALID_BUY`, buys_scored 1, return -0.5; tampered `ABOVE_TOLERANCE_RESIDUAL`, buys_scored 0, quarantine 0, no account for the buy. So no new consequence class, only a false sentence.
findings.why_it_matters: The paragraph is explicitly framed as the accurate replacement for an overclaim ("the residue is stated rather than claimed away"), and it draws a distinction — constructor ran / fields later rewritten — that three ordinary routes do not respect. `copy.copy` in particular is not adversarial code.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace "guarantees that every leg reaching a stage was produced by `Transfer.__init__`" with a statement about type identity only, and note that `object.__new__`, `copy`/`pickle` and `__class__` reassignment all yield `type(x) is Transfer` without `Transfer.__init__` having run — with the consequence set unchanged (sentinel quarantines loudly, mixed-case address drops silently).

findings.title: _rebuilt's "typed refusal rather than an incidental TypeError" does not hold, because _check_payload runs first
findings.measured:
`_rebuilt`'s docstring claims non-owned types are "passed through untouched, so what meets it is this module's own typed refusal rather than an incidental TypeError from calling somebody else's constructor." But `DiagnosticPack.__post_init__` runs `_check_payload(item)` before `_rebuilt(item)`, and `_check_payload` does `[row.value for row in item.rows]` with no type guard.

Constructed input:
    pack = diagnostic_pack([scalar, ranking])
    object.__setattr__(ranking, "rows", ("x",))
    pack.verify()

Measured output: `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'value'` — not `DiagnosticPromotionRefused`, which is what `DiagnosticRanking.__post_init__` raises for the same input at construction time. The rewrite is still refused, so the safety property holds; only the error quality is worse than the docstring states.
findings.why_it_matters: Minor, but this exact distinction — typed refusal vs incidental error — is one the module argues for at length, so a reader may assume the pack preserves it.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard `_check_payload`'s row iteration with an `isinstance(row, DiagnosticRankingRow)` refusal, or drop the sentence's implication that it covers the pack's whole path.

summary: I enumerated 38 distinct behavioural guards introduced or changed by 2672eed (9 in pipeline/inputs.py, 6 in pipeline/run.py, 2 in fifo/matching.py, 20 in reporting/diagnostics.py + reporting/run.py) and probed them with 52 weakenings, each applied to an isolated copy of the tree under /Users/nimaalishahi/scratch-verify and run against the full suite (baseline 1526 passed, 59 skipped). 14 weakenings left the suite fully green. Six of those are behaviourally equivalent mutants (ordering-only changes, and pack-level checks that _rebuilt already re-runs), which I confirmed by constructing distinguishing inputs and finding none. Five are genuine unpinned repairs, and I measured each: three call sites of asset_pairs (pools, token_starts, replacement_pools) can revert to dict() and publish an order-dependent return_pct and an order-dependent §4.7 token-age bucket with the suite green, and DiagnosticRanking's two row guards can both be deleted with the suite green — one lets a duck-typed row through the whole wall and verify(), the other publishes a $1,000 USD figure under a ratio label. Separately, the raw failure counts badly overstate how well the commit is pinned: most failures come from tests/mutations/test_mutation_kills.py reporting that its own anchor text moved, which is a textual pin, not a behavioural one. Stripping those out, six guards — including type(item) is Transfer, which is claim 4 of the commit message — are pinned by exactly one behavioural test each. The repo tree was left clean at 2672eed.

findings.title: asset_pairs' refusal to use dict() is pinned at only one of its four call sites; the other three can revert with the suite green and publish an order-dependent number
findings.measured:
asset_pairs exists so that a caller who supplies a mapping as a *sequence of pairs* cannot have a repeated key collapsed by dict() before asset_keyed sees it. It is called at four sites. Only the prices site is defended.

(a) POOLS. Weakening `supplied = asset_pairs(pools)` to `supplied = tuple(dict(pools).items())` at src/pipeline/run.py:459 -> full suite `1526 passed, 59 skipped` (GREEN, rc=0).
Constructed input: one $1,000 buy of TOKEN_R (4,000 tokens), pool book supplied as pairs with the SAME key twice: `[(TOKEN_R, pool(POOL_R, 1_000*ONE_USDC)), (TOKEN_R, pool(POOL_H, 1_500*ONE_USDC))]`.
  HEAD:     REFUSED ValueError: "pools names 1 asset(s) more than once: 0xc1c1... is named by 2 keys"
  Weakened: PUBLISHED return_pct=-0.2500000000000000
  Weakened, pairs reversed: PUBLISHED return_pct=-0.500000000000000
  Controls (single-entry books): -0.500000000000000 and -0.2500000000000000.
So the published return for one identical input is -25% or -50% depending only on the order of the caller's pairs — exactly the consequence asset_keyed's docstring says it exists to stop.

(b) TOKEN_STARTS. Weakening `starts = asset_pairs(self.token_starts)` to `tuple(dict(self.token_starts).items())` at src/pipeline/inputs.py:351 -> full suite `1526 passed, 59 skipped` (GREEN).
Constructed input: one buy of TOKEN_M one block into the window; `token_starts=[(TOKEN_M, TokenStart(START_BLOCK, START_TS)), (TOKEN_M, TokenStart(START_BLOCK-100_000, START_TS-1_000_000))]`.
  HEAD:     REFUSED ValueError: "token_starts names 1 asset(s) more than once: 0xc2c2..."
  Weakened: PUBLISHED bucket=D, bucket_weights={TokenAgeBucket.D: Decimal('1')}
  Weakened, pairs reversed: PUBLISHED bucket=A, bucket_weights={TokenAgeBucket.A: Decimal('1')}
Bucket A is the first-ten-blocks bucket the Edge Origin condition measures; it flips on caller pair order.

(c) REPLACEMENT_POOLS. Weakening `replacements = asset_pairs(self.replacement_pools)` at src/pipeline/inputs.py:359 -> full suite `1526 passed, 59 skipped` (GREEN).

The only test that covers this class is tests/hand_computed/test_pipeline.py::test_a_price_book_supplied_as_pairs_cannot_smuggle_a_repeat_past_the_check, and it exercises `prices` only. Note that the existing pool-collision test uses `one_pool_book(**{TOKEN_R: p, TOKEN_R.upper(): p})` — a dict with two *distinct* string keys — which dict() does not collapse, so it cannot reach this guard.
findings.why_it_matters: The commit's own repo mutation harness case 49 mutates asset_pairs itself, so the function is defended but three of its four uses are not. A maintainer tidying `_normalised_pools` or `WindowConfig.__post_init__` back to the obvious `dict(...)` spelling gets a green suite and a published return that is a function of the caller's iteration order — the precise failure mode asset_keyed's docstring enumerates.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the pairs-with-a-repeated-key case for `pools`, `token_starts` and `replacement_pools` alongside the existing price-book test — e.g. in tests/properties/test_pipeline.py::test_two_spellings_of_one_asset_in_any_configuration_mapping_are_refused, parametrise over pairs-form inputs as well as dict-form ones, so all four call sites are covered by construction rather than one by name.

findings.title: DiagnosticRanking's row type check is unpinned: deleting it lets a duck-typed row through the ranking, the pack and verify(), with the suite green
findings.measured:
Weakening `if not isinstance(row, DiagnosticRankingRow):` to `if False:` -> full suite `1526 passed, 59 skipped` (GREEN, rc=0).

Constructed input:

    class FakeRow(object):
        rank = 1
        wallet = "0x" + "ff" * 20
        value = DiagnosticValue(amount=Decimal("999999"), kind=USD)

    ranking = DiagnosticRanking(name="absolute_profit_ranking", scope=SCOPE, kind=USD, rows=(FakeRow(),))
    pack = DiagnosticPack(items=(ranking,)); pack.verify()

  HEAD:     REFUSED DiagnosticPromotionRefused: "a FakeRow was placed in a diagnostic ranking. A ranking row carries a payload the gate cannot read..."
  Weakened: ACCEPTED -> FakeRow(rank=1, wallet=..ff.., value=DiagnosticValue(999999, kind='usd'))

The object passes DiagnosticRanking.__post_init__, DiagnosticPack.__post_init__ (both _check_payload and _rebuilt — _rebuilt passes it through untouched because FakeRow is not in _FINAL), and DiagnosticPack.verify(). Nothing in the suite notices.

The TAMPERS table in tests/integration/test_reporting.py (lines 912-949) is otherwise thorough — it has a _DuckScope case for a duck-typed *scope* — but has no duck-typed *row* case, and no test constructs a ranking with a non-row directly.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the type wall the module's docstring calls "the control": "a comment saying so is not a control. Neither is a filter in the gate engine... The control here is the type." The DiagnosticPack docstring lists "a spliced non-diagnostic" among the things verify() catches, but that only covers the pack's own `items`; one level down, in `rows`, the equivalent check is undefended and one deletion from gone.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `_DuckRow` entry to TAMPERS mirroring the existing `_DuckScope` one — `('a ranking row replaced by a duck-typed object', _ranking, lambda r: object.__setattr__(r, 'rows', (_DuckRow(),)))` — which pins it through both test_a_rewritten_diagnostic_cannot_be_published and test_every_tamper_is_also_refused_at_publication_and_not_only_at_collection.

findings.title: DiagnosticRanking's row/ranking kind-agreement check is unpinned: deleting it publishes a dollar figure under a ratio label, with the suite green
findings.measured:
Weakening `if row.value.kind != self.kind:` to `if False:` -> full suite `1526 passed, 59 skipped` (GREEN, rc=0).

Constructed input:

    row = DiagnosticRankingRow(rank=1, wallet=WALLET, value=DiagnosticValue(amount=Decimal("1000"), kind=USD))
    ranking = DiagnosticRanking(name="absolute_profit_ranking", scope=SCOPE, kind=RATIO, rows=(row,))
    pack = DiagnosticPack(items=(ranking,)); pack.verify()

  HEAD:     REFUSED ValueError: "ranking 'absolute_profit_ranking' is reported in ratio and row 1 carries a usd payload; the scale is part of what a reported number means"
  Weakened: ACCEPTED -> (ranking.kind, str(row.value), row.value.kind) == ('ratio', '1000', 'usd')

So $1,000 is published in a record whose declared scale is `ratio`. Note that DiagnosticRankingRow forces its own payload to USD via `_as_payload(self.value, USD, ...)`, so this check is the *only* thing that couples a ranking's declared kind to the scale of the figures inside it.

Why the existing TAMPERS table misses it: it contains `('a ranking row's payload kind rewritten', _ranking, lambda r: object.__setattr__(r.rows[1].value, 'kind', 'ratio'))`, which is caught by `_as_payload` inside DiagnosticRankingRow during _rebuilt (usd vs ratio) rather than by this line. There is no tamper that rewrites the *ranking's own* `kind`.
findings.why_it_matters: The DiagnosticPack docstring explicitly claims verify() catches "a `value.kind` disagreeing with its item's **or its ranking's**". The first half is pinned; the second half is not, and the check that implements it can be deleted without a single test going red. A scale mislabel on a published USD profit ranking is exactly the class of "wrong number that looks plausible" the repository exists to refuse.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `('a ranking's declared kind rewritten', _ranking, lambda r: object.__setattr__(r, 'kind', 'ratio'))` to TAMPERS in tests/integration/test_reporting.py, which pins the line through both the collection-time and publication-time tests.

findings.title: Six guards are pinned by exactly one behavioural test each — including type(item) is Transfer, which is claim 4 of the commit message
findings.measured:
Raw failure counts overstate the pinning badly, because tests/mutations/test_mutation_kills.py fails on "the anchor moved" whenever a mutated line no longer matches its search text. That is a textual pin, not a behavioural one — it goes away the moment someone updates the anchor. Excluding tests/mutations/, the behavioural failure counts are:

  `type(item) is not Transfer` -> `not isinstance(item, Transfer)`  : 15 total failures, 14 of them anchor-moved, 1 behavioural
      the one test: tests/hand_computed/test_pipeline.py::test_a_transfer_subclass_that_skips_the_seam_is_refused
  `_require_one_transaction_per_hash` conditioned on the two rows *disagreeing* rather than on the collision : 15 total, 1 behavioural
      tests/hand_computed/test_pipeline.py::test_the_same_transaction_object_supplied_twice_is_still_two_rows
  `asset_pairs` reading the caller's pairs rather than dict() : 16 total, 1 behavioural
      tests/hand_computed/test_pipeline.py::test_a_price_book_supplied_as_pairs_cannot_smuggle_a_repeat_past_the_check
  fifo `_require_a_total_order`'s case-folding, `(event.tx_hash or "").lower()` -> `event.tx_hash or ""` : 15 total, 1 behavioural
      tests/hand_computed/test_pipeline.py::test_a_bypassed_hash_normalisation_does_not_reach_the_double_count
  `report_run` calling `diagnostics.verify()` at src/reporting/run.py:161 : 6 total, 1 behavioural
      tests/integration/test_reporting.py::test_a_pack_rewritten_after_construction_cannot_be_reported
  `_require_one_transaction_per_hash` running *after* the per-item checks : 2 total, 0 behavioural — pinned ONLY by the mutation harness's anchor for case 43

For contrast, the well-pinned guards: deleting the hash-guard call site produces 11 behavioural failures, `asset_keyed`'s collision refusal 11, Diagnostic's payload wrapping 29.
findings.why_it_matters: `type(item) is Transfer` is one of the six numbered claims of the commit message, and the commit says the class of subclass bypass is now closed. It is closed by one assertion in one test. Delete that test in a future tidy-up and the isinstance regression is silent again. The same applies to the collision-not-disagreement shape of the hash guard, which the commit message and the repo's own mutation case 44 both call out as the papered-over repair worth making expensive.
findings.suggested_fix: For each of the six, add a second assertion at a different level — most cheaply, promote the subclass and duplicate-object cases into tests/properties/test_pipeline.py alongside the existing property tests, and add a `report_run`-level assertion for the verify() call. Also consider that the mutation harness's anchor-moved failures are not evidence of behavioural coverage; the harness's control cases could report behavioural-vs-anchor separately so this is visible.

findings.title: The stated reason for running _check_payload before _rebuilt is not real — the order is behaviourally irrelevant
findings.measured:
Swapping `_check_payload(item)` and `_rebuilt(item)` in DiagnosticPack.__post_init__ -> full suite `1526 passed, 59 skipped` (GREEN), and I could construct no input that distinguishes the two orders.

    d = Diagnostic(name="buy_win_rate", scope=SCOPE, kind=RATIO, value=DiagnosticValue(Decimal("0.61"), RATIO))
    object.__setattr__(d, "value", Decimal("0.61"))     # the exact tamper the ordering is said to protect
    DiagnosticPack(items=(d,))

  HEAD:            REFUSED DiagnosticPromotionRefused: "diagnostic 'buy_win_rate' carries a Decimal payload rather than a DiagnosticValue..."
  Order swapped:   REFUSED DiagnosticPromotionRefused: identical message.

The reason is in the code itself: `_rebuilt` returns a new object which DiagnosticPack.__post_init__ discards, so `_as_payload`'s coercion never touches `item`. The docstring at :600-604 says "a rebuild whose result was kept would launder exactly the tamper `_check_payload` exists to catch. That is why `DiagnosticPack.__post_init__` runs `_check_payload` *before* this." The conditional clause is true; the "that is why" does not follow, because the result is not kept.
findings.why_it_matters: The commit's stated standard is that an overclaimed guarantee is worse than an accurate weaker one, because the next reader relies on it. This is a small instance of exactly that: a reader is told an ordering is load-bearing when it is not, which spends attention in the wrong place and would make a future reordering look dangerous when it is inert.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the comment at :552-554 and the paragraph at :600-604 to say the ordering is for message quality (the bare-Decimal refusal names the actual defect rather than an incidental downstream one), and that the rebuild's result being discarded is what makes the order otherwise immaterial.

findings.title: WindowConfig's lookups moving from .lower() to normalise_asset is unpinned, and so are three redundant diagnostics checks
findings.measured:
Five more weakenings left the suite green (`1526 passed, 59 skipped`). I separated them into one real-but-unreachable difference and four equivalent mutants:

(1) UNPINNED, real API difference, not reachable through the composed pipeline. Reverting `self.token_starts.get(normalise_asset(token))` -> `self.token_starts.get((token or "").lower())` (:374), and the same at :378. Measured:
    c = WindowConfig(horizon_block=100, horizon_ts=1000, token_starts={NATIVE_ETH: TokenStart(1, 1)})
    c.token_starts        -> {'0xc02aaa39b223fe8d0a0e5c4f27ead9083c756cc2'}   (asset_keyed collapsed the sentinel onto WETH)
    HEAD:      c.token_start(NATIVE_ETH) -> TokenStart(block=1, timestamp=1)
    Weakened:  c.token_start(NATIVE_ETH) -> None
  A None §4.7 start quarantines the buy as unknown-age. I could not reach it through run_wallet_window, because Transfer.__post_init__ collapses ETH onto WETH before netting, so `buy.asset` at run.py:716/749 is never the sentinel. It is nonetheless the mirror image of the half-implementation this commit removed (stores normalised, lookups not), and nothing would say so.

(2) EQUIVALENT MUTANTS — deleting them changes no observable behaviour on any input I could construct:
  - `_check_name(item.name)` at :550 and `_check_gate_relevance(item.gate_relevance)` at :551. Tampering name -> 'not_pre_registered' or gate_relevance -> 'GATE' and packing still raises the identical UnknownDiagnostic / DiagnosticPromotionRefused, because `_rebuilt` re-runs Diagnostic.__post_init__ which restates both.
  - `_rebuilt`'s `type(value) not in _FINAL` at :608 loosened to an isinstance test: no proper subclass of a diagnostic type can exist (_Sealed refuses it), so nothing distinguishes them.
  - `DiagnosticValue.__post_init__`'s `if self.kind not in KINDS` at :334: only distinguishable by direct construction (`DiagnosticValue(Decimal('1'), kind='bananas')` -> ACCEPTED vs REFUSED). Reached through a pack, the tamper is still caught by `_as_payload`'s kind-disagreement check.

(3) Two ordering changes are also inert. Moving the cross-entry collision check ahead of the per-entry type check in WindowConfig, and ahead of the per-price positivity check in _normalised_prices, both keep the suite green and both still refuse every input I constructed — only the exception type and which spelling appears in the message change (TypeError naming '0XC1C1...' becomes ValueError naming the collision).
findings.why_it_matters: None of these is a wrong number today. They are recorded because the lens is "a repair no test defends is a repair the next refactor deletes": (1) is a genuine behavioural change made by this commit with zero coverage, and (2) are defence-in-depth layers that are currently invisible — they would become live holes the moment `_rebuilt` or `_Sealed` were touched, and nothing would report that.
findings.suggested_fix: For (1), either add a test asserting `WindowConfig(token_starts={NATIVE_ETH: ...}).token_start(NATIVE_ETH)` resolves (and the same for replacement_pool), or state in the docstring that the sentinel cannot reach these lookups through the composed pipeline, the way the repo's EQUIVALENT table in tests/mutations/test_mutation_kills.py records case E1. For (2), the same EQUIVALENT-with-inverted-assertion treatment would make the redundancy an explicit, falsifiable claim rather than an untested one.
